findings.passage: "Modernizing our firearms statutes is not an attack on anyone's rights," Stoneham Rep. Michael Day, the bill's author said during Wednesday's session.
findings.note: WBUR quotes Day on the House floor while the House passed the firearms overhaul bill.

findings.passage: Day said that change “provides some more clarity, and we think, entrenches it even more firmly on constitutional grounds.”
findings.note: GBH quotes Day on the reworked bill's rule that a gun may not be brought into a home without permission, leaving businesses to set their own policy.
subjects: places where guns may be carried

findings.passage: Day, the House chair of the Judiciary Committee, said the revised bill incorporates feedback heard from activists, gun owners, law enforcement and other state representatives.
findings.note: GBH reports (not a direct quote) what Day said about the revised bill; the outlet paraphrases him.

findings.passage: "One caller among many callers to my office said, 'Now, I'm not a racist, but these guns aren't getting up to shoot themselves.' Always good to start with 'now, I'm not a racist, but...'" Day said.
findings.note: NBC Boston (State House News) quotes Day on the House floor answering opponents of the bill. Article published 2023-10-19, remarks made on the day of the vote.

findings.passage: "That will give our law enforcement folks another leg up to say 'Hey, somebody's out here compiling 50 barrels. What's going on here?' They can take a look at what actually is happening, whether this is now a trafficking situation," Day said.
findings.note: WBUR/State House News quotes Day on the part of his June 2023 bill that tracks gun parts and untraceable guns.

findings.passage: "The licensing laws that we have on the books work, right? We've got the lowest rate of gun deaths in the continental U.S. of all gun deaths," Day told the News Service.
findings.note: Day, on the day his bill was filed, on Massachusetts gun licensing and gun-death rates.

findings.passage: “A year ago, this Legislature responded to the Supreme Court’s attempt to weaken Massachusetts gun safety statutes with a bill from the Joint Committee on the Judiciary. Two weeks ago, I filed a bill that reflects the work that I, and a majority of my colleagues, have done in the wake of that decision.
findings.note: Day's statement (quoted by Commonwealth Beacon) about his June 2023 firearms bill and the Supreme Court Bruen ruling. Date is the article's publication date; the statement was made around then.

findings.passage: Rep. Michael Day and Sen. Cynthia Creem, who have been leading the talks, said just before 1:30 p.m. they will soon file a compromise bill that "delivers meaningfully on our promise to align our statutes with the challenges gun violence poses to our communities today and incorporates the perspectives of firearm owners, law enforcement, community leaders and those impacted directly by gun violence."
findings.note: Joint statement by Day and a Senate co-negotiator on the final compromise firearms bill (date is the article date).
subjects: places where guns may be carried

findings.passage: Day added, "That's just in Massachusetts. Since June one, there have been 107 mass shootings, injuring 576 people and killing 103 people in the United States -- June one to today. So there's your problem that we need to solve. We don't have to live this way."
findings.note: Day, as lead House negotiator, speaking on the House floor before the vote on the final gun bill; quoted by NBC Boston.
